title: SEC7: calibration — round 1
description: Confidence assessment: ~15% chance of a missed bug in the P0 fixes as a whole. The individual fixes are well-scoped and each has a matching test. The highest residual risk is in the suck_pull msgid normalization gap (c3z.5) and the sieve_admin unauthenticated start path (c3z.2) — both filed as separate P1 issues by other reviewers, so they are captured. The admin /stats wrong-pool issue (c3z.8) is pre-existing and not introduced by bt5.9; it lowers confidence in operator observability but not in correctness of the fixes themselves. Opinion findings filed: 0. All findings from other reviewers have engineering basis that would survive a code review comment thread — none are stylistic preferences. Running out of real complaints: no, two real P1 issues (c3z.2, c3z.5) and one P2 (c3z.4) remain open. Good engineering decisions identified: 6 — RFC 2046 boundary termination check, Bearer/Basic fallthrough safety, rate limiter IP keying, admin config validate-at-parse-time, Sieve reject reason sanitization, Sieve compile fail-closed with 4xx deferral, TAKETHIS stream drain on too-large.
